title: Captain Polyplast Ltd - 536974 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Captain Polyplast Q1 FY27 total income rose 16.3% YoY to Rs 81.66 crore, with EBITDA margin up 99 bps to 12.07%.
summary.overview: Management reported Q1 FY27 total income of Rs 81.66 crore (+16.3% YoY), EBITDA of Rs 9.86 crore (+26.7%) and net profit of Rs 4.66 crore with diluted EPS of Rs 0.78. Management said the quarter was hit by geopolitical-driven raw material inflation but revenue growth and margin both improved. Solar EPC order wins of 1,500 pumps in the first four months were highlighted, with 800 already executed and 700 pending. Ahmedabad plant (70,000 sq ft) commenced production, and the company was listed on NSE in July 2026.

segments.name: Micro-irrigation
segments.commentary: Backbone of operations; sales network across 16 states with about 750 dealers. Management targets around Rs 600 crore of micro-irrigation business on existing capacity. Shifting mix toward commercial, non-subsidy and allied products.

segments.name: Solar EPC
segments.commentary: Two verticals: solar water pumping (PM-KUSUM, currently only Maharashtra; empanelled in Maharashtra and Gujarat) and rooftop. Management did not quantify segment revenue or growth; said solar revenue was H2-weighted last year. Targets solar EPC contribution of 50% over next 3 years.

guidance_outlook: Blended EBITDA margin expected to improve about 10-15 bps every quarter as Ahmedabad ramps up; volume growth cited as main margin driver.
Micro-irrigation margin uplift of 1-1.5% expected once Ahmedabad is fully operational, over the next 2-3 years.
Raw material (LLDP/HDPE) prices up about 30-35% versus Jan/Feb levels after a ~50% spike at end-March; price revisions expected to be largely complete by end of Q2, with full benefit from Q3.
Central government price revision mechanism expected by end-September.
Expects working capital to improve by year end as micro-irrigation receivables are collected in H2.
capex_capacity: Ahmedabad facility (70,000 sq ft, Gujarat) commenced production; will in-house valves, connectors and accessories (about 10% of micro-irrigation system value); full replacement of outsourced components expected to take at least 2-3 years.
Existing micro-irrigation capacity across Rajkot, Kurnool and Ahmedabad can support around Rs 600 crore of business; management sees no manufacturing bottleneck.
Solar EPC is service-only; no in-house manufacturing, so growth constrained by execution rather than capacity.
Dedicated solar execution team already set up; limited incremental manpower needed in states with existing micro-irrigation teams.
demand_pricing: Solar pump orders: 500 pumps from MSEDCL in Q1 and 1,000 more in July 2026; 800 of 1,500 executed, 700 pending, expected to be completed by end of August 2026.
Solar rooftop: 60-70% of rooftop business sourced from existing micro-irrigation dealers; solar pumps largely via dedicated solar dealers.
Replacement demand in mature states (Maharashtra, Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu) currently about 10-20% of micro-irrigation demand.
Export growth said to be in line with domestic growth from a very low base; future growth to come from new customers. Africa and Latin America named as focus markets.
Other states' solar tenders expected to be floated around September; awaiting tender release.

qa_highlights.question: Dealer network and scope for expansion in under-penetrated markets?
qa_highlights.answer: Around 750 dealers across 16 states; no need for more dealers in existing states. Expansion focus in Northern/Eastern states (Jharkhand, West Bengal, Bihar, UP).

qa_highlights.question: Current status of 1,500 solar pump order execution?
qa_highlights.answer: 800 completed, 700 pending, expected to be completed by end of the current month.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of polymer prices and price pass-through?
qa_highlights.answer: Raw material prices rose about 50% at end-March and are now up 30-35% vs Jan/Feb. Free-pricing markets have passed on increases; Gujarat revised subsidy prices; other southern states expected in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Solar pump growth outlook and share in business?
qa_highlights.answer: Expects solar EPC to reach 50% of overall business in 3 years; expansion planned to Rajasthan, Jharkhand, Karnataka and Haryana this year.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital cycle for micro-irrigation vs solar pumps?
qa_highlights.answer: Micro-irrigation payment cycle 5-6 months (8-10 months in Andhra Pradesh); solar pump receivable cycle 3-4 months. Majority of working capital sits in receivables, not inventory.

qa_highlights.question: Ahmedabad facility margin benefit and ramp-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Micro-irrigation margin benefit of 1-1.5% when fully operational; blended margin uplift of 10-15 bps each quarter during ramp-up. Initial focus on cost efficiency, standalone sales later.

qa_highlights.question: Export growth drivers?
qa_highlights.answer: Export growth similar to domestic, but from a very low base; meaningful growth requires new customers.

risks_watch: Raw material (polymer) cost inflation and pace of state price revisions, especially Tamil Nadu, Andhra and other southern states.
Working capital intensity rising in Q1-Q2; receivable cycles of 5-10 months for micro-irrigation.
Dependence on state tenders for solar pump expansion beyond Maharashtra and Gujarat; tenders expected around September.
Competitive pricing pressure in solar pumps, per management.
Execution bottleneck in solar pump installation as order book scales; export still a small base.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volumes, order wins and margin trajectory, but cautious on near-term cash flow and tender timing. Several answers were vague on quantification (solar segment revenue, growth comparisons), and the line had multiple audio drops.
key_quotes: So for the solar rooftop business, I can say that majority of our rooftop business is coming from the existing dealer network.
So definitely from Q3, we can see the full impact of that price revision.

adds.what: Ahmedabad plant (70,000 sq ft, Gujarat) commenced production; in-house valves, connectors and accessories (~10% of micro-irrigation system value)

growth.why: Management targets about Rs 600 crore of micro-irrigation business on existing capacity (no bottleneck), with 1,500 solar pump orders (800 executed, 700 pending by end-August) and Q1 total income up 16.3%; no explicit revenue growth % guided, and solar execution is constrained by execution rather than capacity.
